source: English translation: Valmiki Ramayanam, IIT Kanpur (https://www.valmiki.iitk.ac.in/), via the MIT-licensed Valmiki Ramayan Dataset by Ashutosh Vijay.

verses.1: While those two were thus conversing, the revered sage Durvasa, desiring an audience with Rama, approached the royal gate.
verses.2: Having approached Saumitri, the best of sages indeed said, "Show Rama to me quickly, before my purpose passes away."
verses.3: Having heard the words of the sage, Lakshmana, the destroyer of enemy heroes, saluted the great-souled one and then spoke these words.
verses.4: Lakshmana asked, "O revered one, what is the task or purpose, and what shall I do, for Rama is indeed busy, O Brahmana, please wait for a moment."
verses.5: Having heard that, the tiger among sages, agitated by anger, spoke words to Lakshmana as if burning him with his eyes.
verses.6: The sage commanded, "O son of Sumitra, announce me to Rama this very moment; if you do not announce me to Rama this very moment, O son of Sumitra..."
verses.7: ...then I shall curse your kingdom, you, the city, Rama, and also Bharata, O son of Sumitra, and all your progeny.
verses.8: Having heard the terrible words of that great soul, he pondered in his mind the definite meaning of that statement, realizing he could no longer contain his anger.
verses.9: Deciding with his intellect that it was better for one person to die than for everyone to be destroyed, he reported this to Rama.
verses.10: Having heard Lakshmana's words, King Rama dismissed Kala and quickly came out to see the son of Atri.
verses.11: Having saluted the great soul who was blazing with splendor, Rama, with folded hands, asked what his purpose was.
verses.12: Having heard those words spoken by Rama, the best of sages, Durvasa, replied to the lord, saying, "O lover of righteousness, listen."
verses.13: O sinless one, today marks the completion of my thousand-year penance, and so I desire whatever food is ready to break my fast.
verses.14: Having heard that word, King Rama, with a pleased mind, offered food to the chief of sages as it was prepared.
verses.15: Having eaten that nectar-like food, the best of sages praised Rama saying "Excellent, Rama!" and then returned to his own hermitage.
verses.16: After that excellent sage had returned to his hermitage, Rama, the elder brother of Lakshmana, remembered the words of Kala and was then overcome with sorrow.
verses.17: Deeply distressed by sorrow and remembering that terrible sight, he became downcast and dejected, unable to utter a word.
verses.18: Then, the greatly renowned Rama, having intellectually ascertained the words of Kala and deciding that "this is not (to be avoided)", remained silent. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे पञ्चोत्तरशततमः सर्गः ।। 105 ।। Thus ends the hundred and fifth sarga of Uttara Kanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.
